From 67791202c5e069cf2ba51db0718d56c634709e78 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2020 21:06:39 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] ALSA: hda/realtek - Fix unexpected init_amp override

The commit 1c76aa5fb48d ("ALSA: hda/realtek - Allow skipping
spec->init_amp detection") changed the way to assign spec->init_amp
field that specifies the way to initialize the amp.  Along with the
change, the commit also replaced a few fixups that set spec->init_amp
in HDA_FIXUP_ACT_PROBE with HDA_FIXUP_ACT_PRE_PROBE.  This was rather
aligning to the other fixups, and not supposed to change the actual
behavior.

However, this change turned out to cause a regression on FSC S7020,
which hit exactly the above.  The reason was that there is still one
place that overrides spec->init_amp after HDA_FIXUP_ACT_PRE_PROBE
call, namely in alc_ssid_check().

This patch fixes the regression by adding the proper spec->init_amp
override check, i.e. verifying whether it's still ALC_INIT_UNDEFINED.

Fixes: 1c76aa5fb48d ("ALSA: hda/realtek - Allow skipping spec->init_amp detection")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
BugLink: https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=207329
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200418190639.10082-1-tiwai@suse.de
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

diff --git a/sound/pci/hda/patch_realtek.c b/sound/pci/hda/patch_realtek.c
index dc5557d79c43..54e1c9c0a33f 100644
--- a/sound/pci/hda/patch_realtek.c
+++ b/sound/pci/hda/patch_realtek.c
@@ -797,9 +797,11 @@ static void alc_ssid_check(struct hda_codec *codec, const hda_nid_t *ports)
 {
 	if (!alc_subsystem_id(codec, ports)) {
 		struct alc_spec *spec = codec->spec;
-		codec_dbg(codec,
-			  "realtek: Enable default setup for auto mode as fallback\n");
-		spec->init_amp = ALC_INIT_DEFAULT;
+		if (spec->init_amp == ALC_INIT_UNDEFINED) {
+			codec_dbg(codec,
+				  "realtek: Enable default setup for auto mode as fallback\n");
+			spec->init_amp = ALC_INIT_DEFAULT;
+		}
 	}
 }
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `sound/pci/hda/patch_realtek.c`**
- The function `alc_ssid_check` was modified to include a conditional check before overriding the `spec->init_amp` field.
- The line that sets `spec->init_amp` to `ALC_INIT_DEFAULT` was wrapped in an `if` statement that checks if `spec->init_amp` is equal to `ALC_INIT_UNDEFINED`. This ensures that the override only occurs if `init_amp` has not been previously defined.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a regression introduced by a previous commit (1c76aa5fb48d) that altered the behavior of how `spec->init_amp` is assigned. The patch ensures that the initialization logic respects the intended behavior by preventing unintended overrides of `spec->init_amp` after the `HDA_FIXUP_ACT_PRE_PROBE` call, specifically in the context of the `alc_ssid_check` function. This change is crucial for maintaining the correct initialization state for the audio hardware on affected systems, such as the FSC S7020.

Here is the commit message:
ALSA: hda/realtek - Fix unexpected init_amp override

The commit 1c76aa5fb48d ("ALSA: hda/realtek - Allow skipping
spec->init_amp detection") changed the way to assign spec->init_amp
field that specifies the way to initialize the amp.  Along with the
change, the commit also replaced a few fixups that set spec->init_amp
in HDA_FIXUP_ACT_PROBE with HDA_FIXUP_ACT_PRE_PROBE.  This was rather
aligning to the other fixups, and not supposed to change the actual
behavior.

However, this change turned out to cause a regression on FSC S7020,
which hit exactly the above.  The reason was that there is still one
place that overrides spec->init_amp after HDA_FIXUP_ACT_PRE_PROBE
call, namely in alc_ssid_check().

This patch fixes the regression by adding the proper spec->init_amp
override check, i.e. verifying whether it's still ALC_INIT_UNDEFINED.

Fixes: 1c76aa5fb48d ("ALSA: hda/realtek - Allow skipping spec->init_amp detection")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
BugLink: https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=207329
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20200418190639.10082-1-tiwai@suse.de
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a change in the way the `spec->init_amp` field was assigned, specifically by replacing the fixup action from `HDA_FIXUP_ACT_PROBE` to `HDA_FIXUP_ACT_PRE_PROBE`. This change inadvertently allowed the `spec->init_amp` to be overridden in the `alc_ssid_check` function without proper checks, leading to unexpected behavior on certain hardware configurations, such as the FSC S7020.

Here is the patch:
  * ports contains an array of 4 pin NIDs for port-A, E, D and I */
 static void alc_ssid_check(struct hda_codec *codec, const hda_nid_t *ports)
 {
 	if (!alc_subsystem_id(codec, ports)) {
 		struct alc_spec *spec = codec->spec;
-		codec_dbg(codec,
-			  "realtek: Enable default setup for auto mode as fallback\n");
-		spec->init_amp = ALC_INIT_DEFAULT;
+		if (spec->init_amp == ALC_INIT_UNDEFINED) {
+			codec_dbg(codec,
+				  "realtek: Enable default setup for auto mode as fallback\n");
+			spec->init_amp = ALC_INIT_DEFAULT;
+		}
 	}
 }

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
spec->init_amp = ALC_INIT_DEFAULT;
```
Reason:
The assignment of `spec->init_amp` to `ALC_INIT_DEFAULT` occurs unconditionally in the `alc_ssid_check` function, which means that it can override any previous value set during the `HDA_FIXUP_ACT_PRE_PROBE` phase. This behavior can lead to unexpected initialization of the amplifier settings, particularly on specific hardware configurations like the FSC S7020.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (spec->init_amp == ALC_INIT_UNDEFINED) {
    spec->init_amp = ALC_INIT_DEFAULT;
}
```
Reason:
This conditional check ensures that `spec->init_amp` is only set to `ALC_INIT_DEFAULT` if it is still in its undefined state (`ALC_INIT_UNDEFINED`). This prevents the unintended override of the `spec->init_amp` value that may have been set earlier, thus preserving the intended behavior and fixing the regression issue.
